posts.cooked: I would say any five heroes who lack destruction abilities, since this can really screw you up if you're fighting someone who puts out horrible ongoings (or are in an environment with lots of nasty cards) and you then have no way to counter them (or in the case of environment targets must divert resources to deal with them when you could be pounding on the main bad guy). It would probably just end up as something of a damage race, though in some cases the ongoing/environmetn cards would be ones that actively stopped you from doing certain things or otherwise messed up whatever tactics you were trying to use (eg Ra being the main damage-dealer against Omnitron, who then plays an Adaptive Plating Subroutine).

posts.name: Ironic
posts.cooked:
I'd say people are on the right track looking for nothing but "just damage" characters who can't manipulate decks/destroy non-Targets.  However, some characters in that category are amazing - and Legacy, in particular, may well be the most powerful in the game.

 

I'll try to avoid any "control" effects as well, but my real priority is to find heroes who are setup dependant - I've had really effective games with Unity and AZ (I've had each of them win games near-singlehandedly, in fact), but they're also more inconsistant, since they need to draw the right cards, in the right order, without the villain breaking those cards too soon.

Bunker (Freedom Six)

Expatriette (Dark Watch)

Absolute Zero (Termi-Nation)

Mr. Fixer (Dark Watch)

For the last slot, I can't quite decide between Chrono-Ranger (base) and Unity (Termi-Nation).  They each have a tiny amount of stuff destruction, and they both tend to be better at their jobs once they get going than the other four.  Even without setup, Ranger is actually pretty good at single-target damage if there's no reduction about, whilst Unity has some of the highest damage in the game on a good day.  Even still, these characters have much more limited options than many others - any team made using these six can break things, but lacking so many options, they'll lose more Advanced games than they win.

 

Hurm.  I guess I should try a few villains with them, see what I can do.  Let's start with... Citizen Dawn (Advanced).

posts.name: Agent Bon
posts.cooked:
phantaskippy listed some I have to agree with.

GI Bunker is probably the most limited hero I know of.

Dark Watch Setback...  I used just as many times as GI Bunker (1).  Setback can get a lot of milage from his base power and seems a lot worse without it, if nothing else to help him get another power faster.

Redeemer Fanatic would be great at setting up her ultimate attack, though you've been healing a lot.  It seems rather contradictory.  I kind of like it for Miss Information but that's the only time I use this variant.

The rest, I'm a bit indecisive about.

How about the other 2 Bunkers?  I guess the environment might get glued down.  Good luck building up before the villain becomes unmanageable, or if a big equipment destruction card comes along.  If I can't do triple Bunker...

Termi-Nation Absolute Zero adds more necessity to setup, more vulnerability to equipment destruction, and another without much damage on the inherent power.

Base Guise with no one to help him draw or do extra damage doesn't seem to get much done very often.  The team also lacks very many Ongoings worth copying, and a lot of the equipment to borrow wouldn't accomplish much on him.

You might win some games, but it would take you so long to get there.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Legacy is really good, this is true, but say you have him on a team that has no ongoing/environment destruction and you come up against Dawn. Your other heroes can do decent damage and take out the citizens. But then Return with the Dawn comes out. And another copy. And you can't get rid of them. Or Channel the Eclipse (however many copies there are of that), so Dawn keeps playing extra cards to bring out more citizens and is rezzing the dead ones as fast as you can kill them. And two of them are Anvil and Truth, of course. And Sweat and Tears. And there's nothing you can do about it.

Okay that's just one villain out of...however many there are, but think how many villains have a bunch of ongoings that, if left out, can just totally wreck you through either buffing the villain's damage, giving them soak/immunity to stuff, letting them bring out targets. And very few of these ongoings tend to have a "you can do X to destroy this card" thing on them (Miss Info's ones are the only ones I can think of). So you would be stuck with them for the whole game once they came out. Yaaay, Backlash Fields!
